rounds.text: The market capitalisation of ₹ 12.8 Cr suggests a micro-cap entity that may lack the liquidity or institutional oversight required for stable long-term valuation [E3]. While the stock is currently trading at its 52-week high, the complete absence of a dividend yield indicates that shareholders receive no direct cash return on their investment [E4, E5]. Furthermore, the stagnation in quarterly operating margins, which remained flat at 5% year-over-year in June 2026, raises questions about the company's ability to sustain the growth trajectory implied by its current valuation [E25]. Conceded: [E1, E6, E7, E8, E11, E24, E38, E39, E40, E61]. Relying on a DCF model to justify an 89% margin of safety is speculative, especially when the company's actual performance shows a recent lack of margin expansion [E25, E39]. Investors should remain cautious of the risks inherent in a company with such a small market footprint and no history of returning capital to shareholders [E3, E4].

The company’s valuation metrics, while appearing inexpensive, must be weighed against the reality that shareholders receive zero return on their capital through dividends [E4]. Despite the theoretical margin of safety suggested by discounted cash flow models, the stock is currently trading at the absolute ceiling of its 52-week range [E5]. Furthermore, the recent quarterly operating margin has stagnated, showing a decline of 1 percentage point compared to the year-ago quarter [E25]. This contraction in quarterly performance suggests that the historical improvements in operating margins may be losing momentum [E24, E25]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E6, E7, E8, E11, E38, E39, E40, E61]. Investors should remain cautious of a micro-cap entity with a market capitalisation of only ₹ 12.8 Cr, as such small valuations often lack the liquidity or institutional oversight required to sustain long-term growth [E3].

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 1.18x (price ₹ 20.2 on a book value of ₹ 17.1).
The stock sits 100% of the way up its 52-week range (13 low to 20 high).
P/E of 4.46x against a sector benchmark of 20.32x.
P/B of 1.19x against a sector benchmark of 1.51x.
ROA of 10.73% against a sector benchmark of 1.55%.
EV/EBITDA of 3.13x against a sector benchmark of 12.75x.
Operating margin is 6% in TTM against 3% three years earlier (+3 percentage points).
Quarterly operating margin is 5% in Jun 2026 against 5% in the year-ago quarter (-1 percentage points).
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 183 per share against a market price of Rs 20.2.
That leaves a margin of safety of 89.0%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies -13.9% earnings growth, against the 18.0% the base case assumes.
Screen reason (bull side): DCF margin of safety 89%
